items.statement: Assume the homogeneous function LSI Ent_mu(v²)≤2C integral||gradient v||² for every compact C-infinity test on a finite-dimensional real Hilbert/Borel space. Then it holds on every C-infinity f with actual f/gradient L2 and integrable f² log(f²), with the same C. The proof constructs compact smooth cutoffs and uses actual mass, entropy-integrand and genuine-gradient energy limits. Those limits themselves retain arbitrary-measure C2 complete-Hilbert scope without finite dimension. Analytic inputs are a canonical lemma's domain, not new premises for the final source exercise.
assumptions: The source premise is exactly compact C-infinity LSI, not a stronger compact C2 premise.
The canonical domain explicitly requires true smoothness, f/gradient L2 and entropy integrability; the actual source consumer must derive them.
The literal homogeneous formula, including0 log0=0, is retained. Probability, positive mass, canonical RN score and semigroup domains are not assumed or inferred.
